records.literal_gloss: For the director. Of David. A psalm.

en.L: For the director. Of David. A psalm.
en.B: For the music director. Of David. A psalm.
en.R: For the leader of the music. A song by David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1.

decisions.choice: Psalm 40:14-18 is also Psalm 70
decisions.reason: The last five verses of this psalm appear again, with small changes, as Psalm 70. A prayer of thanks (verses 2-11) turns into a cry for help (verses 12-18).

source.text: קַוֺּ֣ה קִוִּ֣יתִי יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥ט אֵ֝לַ֗י וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע שַׁוְעָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Waiting I waited [for] YHWH, and he inclined to me and heard my cry.

en.L: Waiting, I waited for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} inclined to me and heard my cry.
en.B: I waited and kept on waiting for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bent down toward me and listened to my cry for help.
en.R: I waited and waited for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to help me. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leaned down to me and heard me cry out.

decisions.choice: Waiting I waited: I waited long and hard
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled (an infinitive with the same verb), which makes it strong: he waited steadily, with hope fixed on the LORD. The word (qavah) is the waiting of hope (27:14).

decisions.choice: he inclined to me: he bent down to listen
decisions.reason: The verb is used of bending the ear to hear (17:6; 31:3). The LORD stoops to the one who calls.

source.text: וַיַּעֲלֵ֤נִי׀מִבּ֥וֹר שָׁאוֹן֮ מִטִּ֪יט הַיָּ֫וֵ֥ן וַיָּ֖קֶם עַל־סֶ֥לַע רַגְלַ֗י כּוֹנֵ֥ן אֲשֻׁרָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought me up from a pit of roaring, from the mud of the mire, and set on a rock my feet; he made firm my steps.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me up from a pit of roaring, from the mud of the mire, and set my feet on a rock; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made my steps firm.
en.B: He drew me up from the roaring pit, out of the clinging mud; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planted my feet on a rock and steadied my steps.
en.R: He pulled me up out of a deep, noisy pit, out of the sticky mud. He set me on solid rock, so that I could walk without slipping.

decisions.choice: roaring: the din of rushing water, or ruin
decisions.reason: The word (sha'on) means a roar or uproar, as of the sea (65:8). A pit of roaring may be a pit where water rushes, or, from a related root, a pit of ruin.

decisions.choice: the pit and the mire: near to death
decisions.reason: The pit is a picture of the grave and of deadly danger (28:1; 30:4; 88:5); mud in which one sinks is the same picture (69:3, 15). The rock is its opposite: firm, safe ground.

decisions.choice: so that I could walk without slipping
decisions.reason: Readable says what firm steps mean.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֬ן בְּפִ֨י׀שִׁ֥יר חָדָשׁ֮ תְּהִלָּ֪ה לֵֽאלֹ֫הֵ֥ינוּ יִרְא֣וּ רַבִּ֣ים וְיִירָ֑אוּ וְ֝יִבְטְח֗וּ בַּיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he put in my mouth a song new, praise to our God; many will see and fear, and they will trust in YHWH.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put in my mouth a new song, praise to our God; many will see and fear, and they will trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: He gave me a new song to sing, a hymn for our God. Many people will look on and be filled with awe, and they will put their trust in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He gave me a new song to sing, a song that praises our God. Many people will see what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done. They will be amazed, and they will trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a new song: a song for a new act of rescue
decisions.reason: A new song answers something new that God has done (33:3; 96:1; 98:1). Here the LORD himself puts it in the singer's mouth.

decisions.choice: see and fear: a play on words
decisions.reason: "They will see" (yir'u) and "they will fear" (yira'u) sound almost alike. To fear the LORD is to stand in awe of him, which leads here to trust.

decisions.choice: what he has done
decisions.reason: Readable says what the many will see: the rescue of verse 3.

source.text: אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי הַגֶּ֗בֶר אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם יְ֭הֹוָה מִבְטַח֑וֹ וְֽלֹא־פָנָ֥ה אֶל־רְ֝הָבִ֗ים וְשָׂטֵ֥י כָזָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [is] the man who has made YHWH his trust, and has not turned to proud [ones] and [those who] fall away [to] falsehood.

en.L: How blessed [is] {{gender:the person|the man}} who has made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} {{gender:their|his}} trust, and has not turned to the proud, or to those who stray after falsehood!
en.B: How blessed are those who make {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their trust, who do not turn to the arrogant or to those who wander off after lies!
en.R: Life is truly good for people who trust {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They do not follow proud people, or people who turn away to false gods.

decisions.choice: How blessed
decisions.reason: As in 1:1.

decisions.choice: the man: anyone who lives this way
decisions.reason: The word (gever) is a man in his strength, but the blessing is for everyone who trusts the LORD, as in 34:9.

decisions.choice: the proud, falsehood: people who rely on themselves or on lies
decisions.reason: The proud (rehavim) are the arrogant, who trust in themselves. Falsehood (kazav) is a lie; turning aside after it may mean following false gods (Amos 2:4).

decisions.choice: the person, their; "the man", "his" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The words describe anyone who trusts the LORD (m2).

decisions.choice: those, people (plural)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of people in general, which needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: false gods
decisions.reason: Readable takes the falsehood to be false gods (m3).

source.text: רַבּ֤וֹת עָשִׂ֨יתָ׀אַתָּ֤ה׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַי֮ נִֽפְלְאֹתֶ֥יךָ וּמַחְשְׁבֹתֶ֗יךָ אֵ֫לֵ֥ינוּ אֵ֤ין׀עֲרֹ֬ךְ אֵלֶ֗יךָ אַגִּ֥ידָה וַאֲדַבֵּ֑רָה עָ֝צְמ֗וּ מִסַּפֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Many [things] you have done, you, YHWH my God, your wonders and your plans toward us; there is none to compare to you; I would declare and speak [of them]; they are too many to count.

en.L: Many [things] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} plans for us; there is none to compare with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. [If] I would declare and speak [of them], they are too numerous to count.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done so many things, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} plans for us; no one can compare with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! If I tried to tell them all and speak of them, there would be more than I could count.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} my God, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done so many wonderful things for us, and made so many plans for us. No one is like {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! If I tried to tell about all of them, I could never finish.

decisions.choice: your wonders: deeds only God can do
decisions.reason: The word (nifla'ot) is used of God's great acts, above all the rescue from Egypt (9:2; Exodus 3:20).

decisions.choice: none to compare to you
alternatives: they cannot be set out in order before you
decisions.reason: The words may mean that nothing compares with God (89:7), or that his wonders cannot be laid out in order before him, they are so many. Either way the line goes on to say they cannot be counted.

decisions.choice: If (L in brackets)
decisions.reason: The two verbs are a condition without "if": were I to tell them, they would be too many.

source.text: זֶ֤בַח וּמִנְחָ֨ה׀לֹֽא־חָפַ֗צְתָּ אָ֭זְנַיִם כָּרִ֣יתָ לִּ֑י עוֹלָ֥ה וַ֝חֲטָאָ֗ה לֹ֣א שָׁאָֽלְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Sacrifice and offering you did not desire; ears you dug for me; burnt offering and sin offering you did not ask.

en.L: Sacrifice and offering {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not desire — ears {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have dug for me — burnt offering and sin offering {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not ask for.
en.B: You took no pleasure in sacrifice and offering, but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} opened my ears; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did not ask for burnt offerings or sin offerings.
en.R: You did not really want animal sacrifices and gifts. Instead, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made me able to hear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and obey. You did not ask for animals to be burned on the altar or offered for sin.

decisions.choice: ears you dug for me: you made me able to hear and obey
alternatives: you pierced my ear (as a servant for life)
decisions.reason: To dig out ears is to open them, so that a person truly listens; in Hebrew to hear is also to obey (1 Samuel 15:22). Some see the ear of a servant pierced at the door as a mark of service for life (Exodus 21:6), but that uses a different word.

decisions.choice: sacrifice you did not desire: obedience comes first
decisions.reason: The four words cover the main offerings of the law. The psalm does not reject them; it says that what God wants first is a listening, willing heart (1 Samuel 15:22; 51:18-19; Hosea 6:6).

decisions.choice: Hebrews 10:5-7: a body you prepared for me
decisions.reason: Hebrews 10:5-7 quotes verses 7-9 as the words of Christ coming into the world, from the ancient Greek translation, which reads "a body you prepared for me" instead of "ears you dug for me". The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: made me able to hear you and obey
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

source.text: אָ֣ז אָ֭מַרְתִּי הִנֵּה־בָ֑אתִי בִּמְגִלַּת־סֵ֝֗פֶר כָּת֥וּב עָלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Then I said, Here I have come; in [the] scroll of [the] book [it is] written concerning me.

en.L: Then I said, "Look, I have come; in the scroll of the book [it is] written concerning me.
en.B: Then I said, "Here I come! What I must do is written down for me in the scroll of the book.
en.R: So I said, "I am here; I have come. The scroll of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} book tells me what I must do.

decisions.choice: written concerning me: written for me to do
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean what is prescribed for a person, as in 2 Kings 22:13, "all that is written concerning us", which suits verse 9. Hebrews 10:7 hears it as "written about me".

decisions.choice: the scroll of the book: God's written instruction
decisions.reason: Books were written on scrolls. Here it is most likely the law of God (verse 9), which a king was to keep by him and read (Deuteronomy 17:18-19).

decisions.choice: the speech runs into verse 9
decisions.reason: What the psalmist said continues to the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: your book
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear it is God's book (m2).

records.literal_gloss: To do your will, my God, I delight, and your instruction [is] in [the] midst of my inner parts.

en.L: To do {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will, my God, I delight, and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction [is] within my inmost being."
en.B: My God, I love to do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} instruction is deep inside me."
en.R: My God, I am glad to do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want. Your teaching is deep inside me."

decisions.choice: instruction
decisions.reason: As in 1:2 (torah).

decisions.choice: in the midst of my inner parts: in my heart
decisions.reason: The inner parts (me'im) are the deepest self, where feeling and will are. The instruction is not only on a scroll but taken to heart (37:31; Jeremiah 31:33).

decisions.choice: Hebrews 10:7
decisions.reason: Hebrews 10:7-9 ends its quotation with "to do your will, O God" and sees it fulfilled in Christ.

source.text: בִּשַּׂ֤רְתִּי צֶ֨דֶק׀בְּקָ֘הָ֤ל רָ֗ב הִנֵּ֣ה שְׂ֭פָתַי לֹ֣א אֶכְלָ֑א יְ֝הוָ֗ה אַתָּ֥ה יָדָֽעְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: I have told good news [of] righteousness in [the] great assembly; look, my lips I do not hold back; YHWH, you know.

en.L: I have told the good news of righteousness in [the] great assembly; look, my lips I do not hold back; {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know.
en.B: In the great assembly I have announced the good news of righteousness. I have not held my lips back; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know it, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: When {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people met together, I told them the good news that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do what is right. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} know that I did not keep quiet.

decisions.choice: told good news
decisions.reason: The verb (bisser) is to bring good news, as a messenger does (Isaiah 40:9; 52:7).

decisions.choice: righteousness: God's right acts of rescue
decisions.reason: The righteousness he announces is the LORD's: his faithful, just way of putting things right by saving his people (verse 11).

decisions.choice: the great assembly: the people gathered for worship
that you do what is right
decisions.reason: Readable says whose righteousness it is (m2).

source.text: צִדְקָתְךָ֬ לֹא־כִסִּ֨יתִי׀בְּת֬וֹךְ לִבִּ֗י אֱמוּנָתְךָ֣ וּתְשׁוּעָתְךָ֣ אָמָ֑רְתִּי לֹא־כִחַ֥דְתִּי חַסְדְּךָ֥ וַ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ לְקָהָ֥ל רָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: Your righteousness I have not hidden in [the] midst of my heart; your faithfulness and your salvation I have spoken; I have not concealed your loyal love and your truth from [the] great assembly.

en.L: Your righteousness I have not hidden within my heart; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithfulness and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation I have spoken; I have not concealed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth from [the] great assembly.
en.B: Your justice I did not keep shut up in my heart; I talked of how faithful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are and how {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rescue. Your loyal love and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth I did not hide from the great assembly.
en.R: I did not keep to myself how good and fair {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. I told people that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are faithful and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save. I did not hide {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people when they gathered.

decisions.choice: loyal love: faithful, covenant love
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith within a bond, here the LORD's love for his people. Literal and Balanced say "loyal love", Readable "faithful love".

decisions.choice: not hidden, not concealed: openly told
decisions.reason: Saying what he did not do is a strong way of saying what he did: he told it all, out loud. The verse takes up "I do not hold back" from verse 10.

decisions.choice: faithfulness, truth: God can be relied on
decisions.reason: Both words ('emunah, 'emet) come from the root of "amen": what is firm and holds.

source.text: אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָ֗ה לֹא־תִכְלָ֣א רַחֲמֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּ֑נִּי חַסְדְּךָ֥ וַ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ תָּמִ֥יד יִצְּרֽוּנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: You, YHWH, will not withhold your compassion from me; your loyal love and your truth continually will guard me.

en.L: You, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, will not withhold {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} compassion from me; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth will continually guard me.
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, will not hold back {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tender mercy from me; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth will guard me always.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not stop being kind to me. Your faithful love and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} truth will always keep me safe.

decisions.choice: withhold: a play on verse 10
decisions.reason: The verb (kala') is the one in verse 10: he did not hold back his lips, and the LORD will not hold back his compassion.

decisions.choice: will not withhold, will guard: trust, or a prayer
alternatives: do not withhold ...; may your loyal love guard me
decisions.reason: The verbs can be read as confident statements or as requests. Both fit the turn to prayer in the next verses.

decisions.choice: compassion: tender, motherly mercy
decisions.reason: The word (rachamim) is related to the word for the womb.

source.text: כִּ֤י אָפְפ֥וּ־עָלַ֨י׀רָע֡וֹת עַד־אֵ֬ין מִסְפָּ֗ר הִשִּׂיג֣וּנִי עֲ֭וֺנֹתַי וְלֹא־יָכֹ֣לְתִּי לִרְא֑וֹת עָצְמ֥וּ מִשַּֽׂעֲר֥וֹת רֹ֝אשִׁ֗י וְלִבִּ֥י עֲזָבָֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: For evils have surrounded me until [there is] no number; my iniquities have overtaken me, and I am not able to see; they are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has forsaken me.

en.L: For evils have surrounded me beyond number; my iniquities have overtaken me, and I am not able to see; they are more than the hairs of my head, and my heart has forsaken me.
en.B: Troubles too many to count have closed in around me; my sins have caught up with me, and I cannot see. They outnumber the hairs on my head, and my courage has left me.
en.R: So many troubles are all around me that I cannot count them. My sins have caught up with me, and I cannot see where to go. They are more than the hairs on my head. I have lost all courage.

decisions.choice: evils, iniquities: troubles and the sins behind them
decisions.reason: The evils (ra'ot) are troubles that come on him; his iniquities ('avonot) are his own sins, which can also mean the punishment they bring. He does not separate the two.

decisions.choice: I am not able to see: I am overwhelmed
decisions.reason: Not being able to see may mean that troubles hide everything else, or that his eyes fail from weakness and grief (38:11).

decisions.choice: my heart has forsaken me: my courage is gone
decisions.reason: The heart is the inner self; when it leaves, strength and courage go too (38:11).

decisions.choice: where to go
decisions.reason: Readable gives one sense of not being able to see (m2).

source.text: רְצֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה לְהַצִּילֵ֑נִי יְ֝הוָ֗ה לְעֶזְרָ֥תִי חֽוּשָׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: Be pleased, YHWH, to deliver me; YHWH, to my help hurry.

en.L: Be pleased, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to rescue me; {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hurry to my help!
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be willing to rescue me! {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hurry and help me!
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please save me! {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, come quickly and help me!

decisions.choice: Psalm 70:2
decisions.reason: Verses 14-18 are repeated as Psalm 70 (70:2-6), where the first line begins with "God" and lacks "be pleased".

decisions.choice: be pleased: be willing, accept
decisions.reason: The verb (ratsah) is used of God accepting a person or an offering with favor.

source.text: יֵ֘בֹ֤שׁוּ וְיַחְפְּר֨וּ׀יַחַד֮ מְבַקְשֵׁ֥י נַפְשִׁ֗י לִסְפּ֫וֹתָ֥הּ יִסֹּ֣גוּ אָ֭חוֹר וְיִכָּלְמ֑וּ חֲ֝פֵצֵ֗י רָעָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: May they be ashamed and abashed together, those who seek my life to snatch it away; may they be turned back and humiliated, those who desire my harm.

en.L: May they be ashamed and abashed together, those who seek my life to snatch it away; may they be turned back and humiliated, those who desire my harm.
en.B: Let those who hunt for my life to snatch it away be shamed and confounded, all of them; let those who wish me harm be driven back and humiliated.
en.R: Some people are trying to kill me. Make all of them ashamed and confused. Some people want to hurt me. Make them turn back in shame.

decisions.choice: may they be ashamed: a prayer against enemies
decisions.reason: The verbs are wishes. He asks that their plans fail and that they be shown up, the shame they meant for him falling on them (35:4, 26).

decisions.choice: seek my life: try to kill me
decisions.reason: As in 35:4.

decisions.choice: Make them ...
decisions.reason: Readable puts the wishes as requests to the LORD.

source.text: יָ֭שֹׁמּוּ עַל־עֵ֣קֶב בָּשְׁתָּ֑ם הָאֹמְרִ֥ים לִ֝֗י הֶ֘אָ֥ח׀הֶאָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: May they be appalled because of their shame, those who say to me, Aha, aha!

en.L: May they be appalled on account of their shame, those who say to me, "Aha! Aha!"
en.B: Let those who jeer at me, "Aha! Aha!", be stunned by their own shame.
en.R: Some people laugh at me and say, "Ha! Ha!" Let them be shocked when they are put to shame.

decisions.choice: Aha, aha: a gloating laugh
decisions.reason: The cry is the glee of enemies at someone's fall (35:21, 25; Ezekiel 25:3).

decisions.choice: appalled because of: stunned as the reward of
decisions.reason: The verb (shamem) means to be stunned or laid waste; "because of" ('eqev) is "as the result of": their own shame comes back on them.

source.text: יָ֘שִׂ֤ישׂוּ וְיִשְׂמְח֨וּ׀בְּךָ֗ כָּֽל־מְבַ֫קְשֶׁ֥יךָ יֹאמְר֣וּ תָ֭מִיד יִגְדַּ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה אֹֽ֝הֲבֵ֗י תְּשׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: May they exult and rejoice in you, all who seek you; may they say continually, Great [is] YHWH, those who love your salvation.

en.L: May they exult and rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, all who seek {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; may they say continually, "Great is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!" those who love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation.
en.B: But may everyone who looks for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} shout for joy and find gladness in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; may those who love to see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save never stop saying, "How great {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is!"
en.R: But let all who come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} be happy and glad because of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. Let all who love it when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save them always say, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is great!"

decisions.choice: Great is the LORD: praise, or a wish
decisions.reason: The verb can be read as a wish, "may the LORD be great", that is, be shown and praised as great (35:27). Said by those he has saved, it is praise.

decisions.choice: those who seek you: those who turn to God in worship and prayer
decisions.reason: To seek the LORD is to come to him for help and to worship him (9:11; 24:6).

decisions.choice: But
decisions.reason: The wish for those who seek the LORD is set against the wish for the enemies.

source.text: וַאֲנִ֤י׀עָנִ֣י וְאֶבְיוֹן֮ אֲדֹנָ֪י יַחֲשָׁ֫ב לִ֥י עֶזְרָתִ֣י וּמְפַלְטִ֣י אַ֑תָּה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗י אַל־תְּאַחַֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [am] afflicted and needy; [the] Lord will think of me; my help and my deliverer [are] you; my God, do not delay.

en.L: But I [am] poor and needy; may [the] Lord think of me. My help and my deliverer [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; my God, do not delay!
en.B: As for me, I am poor and in need; may the Lord keep me in mind. You are the one who helps me and sets me free; my God, do not be slow!
en.R: I am poor and in need. May the Lord remember me. You help me and save me. My God, please come quickly!

decisions.choice: afflicted and needy: helpless and dependent on God
decisions.reason: As in 35:10; the pair describes those who have no help but the LORD.

decisions.choice: will think of me: may he think of me
decisions.reason: The verb can be a statement or a wish. Psalm 70:6 has "God, hurry to me" here.

decisions.choice: the Lord
decisions.reason: Here the title 'Adonai, "Lord" or "my Lord", is used, not the divine name.
